loi.label: Loi ordinaire
loi.note: Standard statute. Section and Sous-section act as higher divisions, not basic units. Article is the basic citable unit throughout. Alinéa (unnumbered paragraph) is the primary subdivision within articles.

loi_organique.label: Loi organique
loi_organique.note: Organic laws fill in constitutional details. Same structure as loi ordinaire but with constitutional status. Must be validated by Conseil constitutionnel before promulgation. Simpler hierarchy (no Livre/Section typically).

ordonnance.label: Ordonnance
ordonnance.note: Executive ordinances issued under Article 38 delegation from Parliament, or Article 92/74 in overseas territories. Must be ratified by Parliament within stipulated period. Numbered in same sequence as decrets.

decret.label: Décret
decret.note: Decrets en Conseil d'Etat (signed after mandatory Conseil d'Etat opinion) and decrets simples. Presidential decrets (Article 13) signed by President and countersigned by PM. Simpler hierarchy than primary legislation — often just articles.

arrete.label: Arrêté
arrete.note: Ministerial or prefectoral orders implementing decrets. Typically short — mostly just articles. Arretes interministeriels signed by multiple ministers. Rarely codified.

constitution.label: Constitution
constitution.note: Constitution of 4 October 1958. 16 Titres, 89 Articles. Articles numbered continuously through all Titres. No Chapitres at constitutional level. Preamble references the 1946 Constitution preamble and 1789 Declaration.

code.label: Code

hcontainers.name: sous-paragraphe
hcontainers.description: Rare fourth-level division in some codes, below Sous-section

code.note: French codes (Code civil, Code penal, Code du travail, etc.) use a distinctive article numbering scheme: L.xxx-x (legislative part), R.xxx-x (regulatory/decret en CE), D.xxx-x (decret simple). Article numbers encode their position in the hierarchy (e.g., L.1234-5 = Livre 1, Titre 2, Chapitre 3, Art. 4 no. 5). Codification performed by DILA. Codes are maintained at legifrance.gouv.fr as consolidated versions.

frbr.note: French law numbers follow the pattern YYYY-NNN (e.g., loi n° 2023-270). The JORF number is the canonical publication reference. Codes are identified by their conventional short name slug (code-civil, code-penal, code-du-travail).

numbering.note: Laws are cited by their number and publication date: 'Loi n° 2023-270 du 14 avril 2023'. In codes, inserted articles use hyphen notation: after art. L.123-4 comes L.123-4-1, L.123-4-2. Article numbering in codes encodes hierarchical position.

enacting_formulae.text:
L'Assemblée nationale et le Sénat ont adopté,
Le Président de la République promulgue la loi dont la teneur suit :
enacting_formulae.note: Standard promulgation formula for ordinary laws under the Fifth Republic. Signed by President, countersigned by Premier ministre and relevant ministers.
Organic law formula; includes mandatory Conseil constitutionnel conformity declaration.

enacting_formulae.text:
Le Président de la République,
Sur le rapport du Premier ministre et des ministres [portfolios],
Vu l'article 38 de la Constitution,
[...]
Ordonne :
enacting_formulae.note: Ordonnance issued under Article 38 delegation. VISA block lists authorizing law, Conseil d'Etat opinion, Conseil des ministres deliberation.

amendments.phrasing: est ainsi rédigé... est complété par... est abrogé... est remplacé par...
amendments.note: French amendments quote the new text in full ('est ainsi rédigé'). Repeal uses 'est abrogé'. Cross-references cite by number and date: 'la loi n° 2023-270 du 14 avril 2023'. Within codes, articles are cited by their L./R./D. number.

structuring.prompt_additions: French law uses Article as the basic unit (ARTICLE keyword). Higher divisions are Livre (BOOK), Titre (TITLE), Chapitre (CHAPTER), Section (SECTION), Sous-section (SUBSECTION) — all higher divisions, not basic units. Alinéa is an unnumbered paragraph subdivision within an article; use PARAGRAPH keyword. In codes, article numbers encode hierarchy position (L.xxx-x, R.xxx-x, D.xxx-x) — preserve these exactly as the article number. Do not confuse Section (a higher division) with section in the Anglophone sense.

supranational_memberships.note: France is a founding EU member (Treaty of Rome 1957). EU Regulations apply directly; Directives require transposition into French law, typically by loi or ordonnance.

France ratified the ECHR in 1974. ECHR applies in French courts; Cour de cassation and Conseil d'Etat apply it directly. Conseil constitutionnel does not incorporate ECHR into its review (contrôle de conventionnalité is separate from contrôle de constitutionnalité).

display.note: French legislation uses inline headings (not marginal notes). Article headings appear on the same line or immediately above the article text, not in a side margin. Section/Chapitre headings are centred and in small capitals in the JORF typesetting.
